title: A relative color's hue keyword is typed as an angle, so `tan(h)` computes in degrees and `calc(h + 10)` stays unresolved

regression.commit: 4ebcb45 Update relative color parsing to latest spec (#465)

impact: Reported as an agent-style spec deviation (tan(h), min(h, 10deg) are fringe), but the same root cause breaks the ordinary hue-rotation idiom `hsl(from <static color> calc(h + 180) s l)` / `oklch(from #369 l c calc(h + 120))`: since 1.30.0 it is no longer resolved, and with targets lacking relative color syntax (e.g. safari 15) it is no longer lowered, so the color is invalid in those browsers. 1.28.0-1.29.3 lowered it correctly. With a var() origin nothing changes (never lowerable). No reactions or duplicates.
code: src/values/color.rs: define_colorspace! for HSL, HWB, LCH, OKLCH declare `h: Angle` -> ColorSpace::types() gives ChannelType::Angle
src/values/color.rs: RelativeComponentParser::parse_angle_or_number maps an Angle-typed keyword to Calc::Value(Angle::Deg)
src/lib.rs ~20146/20164: tests enshrine the wrong behavior (`calc(h + 180deg)` folds; `sin(h)` expected .451575 = sin(deg), was .990043 = sin(rad) before #465)
summary: CSS Color 5 makes every relative-color channel keyword, including the hue `h`, a <number> ("90 is equivalent to 90deg"). #465 retyped percentage channels as numbers but left hue channels typed as <angle>, so `calc(h + 180)` (number + angle) fails to resolve and is passed through unresolved/unlowered, `calc(h + 180deg)` and `min(h, 10deg)` (invalid in browsers) fold to a valid color, and `sin(h)`/`tan(h)` treat the hue as degrees instead of radians.
repro: triage/sweep/1395-repro.mjs. `.a{color:hsl(from red calc(h + 180) s l)}` -> master/1.30.0+: unchanged; 1.29.3: `.a{color:#0ff}`. With targets safari 15, `oklch(from #336699 l c calc(h + 120))` -> master: `oklch(from #369 l c calc(h + 120))`; 1.29.3: `lab(40.7852% 32.3122 7.46881)`. `lch(from red l c tan(h))` -> master `.864935` (tan of degrees), 1.29.3 `.0169517`.
evidence: repro.mjs on local (= master), 1.33.0, 1.32.0, 1.31.1 and --range 1.27.0..1.33.0: hue-plus-number / lowering / tan(h) correct in 1.28.0-1.29.3, wrong from 1.30.0; calc(h + 10deg) and min(h, 10deg) fold in every version; plain `h` and `calc(l + 10)` correct on master (the latter was wrong before 1.30.0). Only #465 touched color.rs/calc.rs in v1.29.3..v1.30.0. Chromium 153 (probe.mjs): `lch(from red l c tan(h))` -> hue 0.015311 (radians); `calc(h + 10)` -> 50.856; `calc(h + 10deg)` and `min(h, 10deg)` invalid (computed rgb(0,0,0) default / earlier declaration wins); `hsl(from red calc(h + 180) s l)` -> color(srgb 0 1 1). Spec: css-color-5 Overview.bs: "h is a <<number>> that corresponds to the origin color's HSL hue, in degrees ... 90 is equivalent to 90deg" (same for hwb() and lch() h).

fix.approach: Declare hue channels as `h: Number` in define_colorspace! for HSL, HWB, LCH and OKLCH so the keyword becomes Calc::Number (then calc(h + 180) resolves, trig takes radians, mixing with angles is rejected); drop the now-dead Angle branches in parse_angle_or_number. Update the enshrined tests: `lch(from indianred l c calc(h + 180deg))` should no longer fold (browsers reject it), `sin(h)` back to .990043; add `calc(h + 180)` and a lowering test with targets. Note behavior change: CSS that relied on the invalid `calc(h + 180deg)` folding will now pass through (and be invalid in browsers, as it already is unminified).

draftReply:
Thanks, confirmed, and it's a regression: since 1.30.0 the hue keyword in relative colors is treated as an angle, while CSS Color 5 defines it as a number ("90 is equivalent to 90deg"). Besides `tan(h)`, this affects the common hue-rotation form: `hsl(from red calc(h + 180) s l)` was resolved to `#0ff` in 1.29.3 but is now left as is, so it's no longer lowered for browsers without relative color support (e.g. `targets: safari 15`). Chromium agrees with the spec on all four of your cases. Until it's fixed, a static origin with `calc(h + 180deg)` still gets lowered, but browsers reject that form, so only use it if the output is always lowered.
